item.title: Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean Set for Fugees Reunion at Global Citizen Live: Rio De Janeiro
item.description:
[Intro music plays]
Host: "Welcome to our show, where we bring you the latest news and trends in music. Today, we're talking about a major reunion that's happening next month in Brazil. Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean, co-founders of the legendary hip-hop group Fugees, are reuniting for a special concert on Ipanema Beach. They're celebrating the 30th anniversary of their iconic album, The Score."
[Cut to music clip: "Killing Me Softly" by Fugees]
Host: "Released in 1996, The Score was a game-changer, debuting at number one on the Billboard 200 and winning the Grammy for Best Rap Album in 1997. The album featured hits like 'Ready or Not', 'Fu-Gee-La', and 'No Woman, No Cry'. And now, Lauryn Hill and Wyclef Jean are coming together again to perform these classic tracks."
[Cut to interview clip: Wyclef Jean]
Wyclef Jean: "We can't think of a better way to celebrate 30 years of The Score than taking action to make the world a better place, together with the beautiful people of Rio de Janeiro."
Host: "The concert is part of Global Citizen's Rio Nature & Climate Week, and it's free, but you have to earn your tickets by taking action on the Global Citizen app or volunteering in the local community. The event will also feature other artists, including YG Marley, Zion Marley, and Latin Grammy winner Ludmilla."
[Cut to interview clip: Ludmilla]
Ludmilla: "Music has this power to connect everyone, and this is a chance to use that to talk about what really matters, which is our world and the future of the next generations."
Host: "So mark your calendars for June 6th and get ready for an unforgettable night of music and activism on Ipanema Beach. Visit globalcitizen.org for more information on how to earn your free tickets. That's all for today's show. Thanks for tuning in!"
[Outro music plays]
